question: Which categories of machinery always require a conformity assessment procedure involving a notified body?
text: Under Directive 2006/42/EC (in force today), Annex IV categories need a notified body only if the machine was not built to the harmonised standards (Art. 12(3)-(4)); no category always needs one. Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 Annex I, Part A would list such categories, but it applies only from 20 January 2027.

question: Which conformity assessment procedures can the manufacturer choose for machinery listed in Annex I, Part A?
value: EU type-examination (module B) followed by conformity to type based on internal production control (module C)
conformity based on full quality assurance (module H)
conformity based on unit verification (module G)
text: Under Article 25(2) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, for machinery listed in Annex I, Part A the manufacturer may apply module B followed by module C, module H, or module G. Module B and C are in Annexes VII and VIII, module H in Annex IX, and module G in Annex X. The Regulation applies from 20 January 2027.

question: Which category does a safety component with self-evolving behaviour based on machine learning fall under?
value: Annex I, Part A, point 5 of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 (the Machinery Regulation): it is in the category of machinery or related products requiring a third-party conformity assessment under Article 25(2).
text: REG.md, Annex I, Part A, point 5 places safety components with fully or partially self-evolving behaviour using machine learning approaches ensuring safety functions in Part A (the Article 25(2) procedures, i.e. third-party conformity assessment). Recital 54 gives the same reason for third-party assessment.

question: When must guards for moving transmission parts be interlocking movable guards instead of fixed guards?
value: Interlocking movable guards are required (under Directive 2006/42/EC, Annex I, 1.3.8.1, which says 'should') where frequent access is envisaged; otherwise a fixed guard may be used.

The successor Regulation, Annex I, section 1.3.8.1, uses 'shall' for the same condition.

question: Who is considered the manufacturer after a substantial modification of machinery?
value: The natural or legal person who carries out the substantial modification of the machinery (not the original manufacturer, unless it is a non-professional user modifying for own use).
text: Under Article 18 of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 (Machinery Regulation), the person who carries out a substantial modification of machinery is considered to be the manufacturer and must meet the manufacturer's obligations under Article 10 for that machinery; a non-professional user modifying for their own use is excluded.
